profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 44 (QTS missing-address campaign): matched a generic row sharing this campus name to the one confirmed unified campus address rather than guessing which of two bookend buildings it represents.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] QTS Data Centers, formerly QTS Realty Trust, is a large scale data center provider. Per Blackstone Real Estate Income Trusts own press release, Blackstone affiliated funds completed a roughly 10 billion dollar acquisition of QTS Realty Trust on August 31, 2021, taking the company private. This specific row is one of three entries in this registry all named QTS Ashburn Lockridge, clustered within about 100 meters of each other. A Baxtel listing for this campus, fetched fresh this session, gives 44675 Quality Tech Lane as the address for the Lockridge ASH2 campus, describing two bookend buildings, ASH2 DC1 and ASH2 DC2, on a 28 acre infill site at that same general location. Given the operators own naming does not carry separate street addresses for the two buildings, this session applied the one confirmed campus address to all three rows sharing this generic Lockridge name.

profile.regional_context: QTS was founded in 2003 by Chad Williams, went public via IPO in 2013, and was acquired by Blackstone (via Blackstone Infrastructure Partners and BREIT) for approximately $10 billion, completed August 31, 2021. QTS is headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas.
profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Northern Virginia campus, spanning Loudoun County (Ashburn-Shellhorn, Ashburn-Moran, Ashburn Lockridge buildings), Prince William County (Manassas DC1, DC2, DC5), and Sterling (Ashburn 1, Ashburn 2). Northern Virginia is confirmed by Wikipedia as one of QTS's primary operating regions, alongside the separate Richmond, VA campus recorded elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
The QTS Ashburn Lockridge campus is a 24-acre, 2-building site in Sterling, Virginia with 75 MW of planned capacity according to the operator's specification. Assuming 40 kW per rack as a conservative estimate for AI training density, this 75 MW translates to roughly 1,875 racks. At 8 accelerators per rack, a common configuration, this implies capacity for approximately 15,000 GPUs at full utilization, though the published specifications do not itemize the actual equipment mix or confirm AI workloads will occupy the site.

The campus is one of several QTS facilities spread across Northern Virginia, clustered in Loudoun County and Prince William County alongside separate facilities in Richmond. Virginia's published data center capacity totals 1,375 MW across 23 facilities with disclosed specifications. At 75 MW, Ashburn Lockridge ranks 24th among Virginia's published facilities, placing it just outside the state's largest disclosed capacity sources. The state contains 326 mapped facilities overall, of which fewer than 7 percent publish power figures.

QTS was acquired by Blackstone Infrastructure Partners and BREIT in August 2021 for approximately $10 billion and operates as a private company. The Ashburn Lockridge campus address and capacity figures come from the operator's own published specifications. Certifications and specific power delivery infrastructure at this site are not published in the available sources.
